extra.message: getDeserializeData() base64-decodes the 'user' cookie and passes it to node-serialize's unserialize(). node-serialize supports IIFE-based function payloads (`_$$ND_FUNC$$_function(){...}()`), so an attacker who controls the 'user' cookie (not signed, not integrity-protected, httpOnly per user.js:setProfileCookie but freely forgeable by an attacker as a client cookie) can achieve arbitrary code execution, e.g. child_process.execSync. Reached via controllers/usersController.js:201-213 (deserialization) and routes/users/user.js:177 (req.cookies). The code comment itself documents a working RCE payload.

authenticateUser() builds a SQL query by directly concatenating the user-supplied email and password into the query string ('SELECT * FROM users WHERE email =\'' + parameter[0] + '\' AND password = \'' + parameter[1] + '\''), then executes it with executeQuery() (no parameterization). Reached from the login form via utils/passportLocalStrategy.js -> controllers/usersController.js:28-38, allowing authentication bypass via SQL injection (e.g. `' OR '1'='1`).

findUserById() concatenates the id parameter directly into 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE id =' + parameter[0] + ';' with no parameterization or type checking. Reached via req.query.id in routes/users/user.js:28 (errorBasedSqli, GET /error-based-sqli) and line 205 (idorUpdateProfile/idorViewProfile), enabling classic/error-based SQL injection.

searchByName() concatenates the username directly into a LIKE clause ('...where username like \'%' + username + '%\';') with no parameterization. Reached via req.body.username in routes/users/user.js:54 (POST /blind-sqli -> usersController.js:52-69 searchByName, no filtering at all) and line 79 (second-order SQLi, using the already-stored req.user.username), enabling blind and second-order SQL injection.

pingMe() builds a shell command via string concatenation ('ping -c 3 ' + ip) and executes it with child_process.exec(), with no sanitization/allow-listing of `ip`. Reached via req.body.ip in routes/users/user.js:135 -> controllers/usersController.js:127-141 (commandInjection). An attacker can supply e.g. `127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd` to execute arbitrary OS commands.

readDosAndDonts() joins the raw user-supplied `filename` into a filesystem path with path.join(__dirname, filename) and reads it with fs.readFile(), with no validation that the resolved path stays under __dirname. Reached via req.query.filename in routes/users/user.js:144 -> controllers/usersController.js:143-157 (arbitraryFileRetrieval). An attacker can supply `../../../../etc/passwd` to read arbitrary files on the filesystem, and the file contents are then reflected unescaped into arbitrary-file-retrieval.ejs:44.

parseXML() parses fully attacker-controlled XML with libxmljs using parserOptions `{ noent: true }`, which enables XML entity substitution. Combined with no DOCTYPE/entity restriction, this allows classic XXE (e.g. `<!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]>`) to read local files or trigger SSRF via external entities. Reached via req.body.search in routes/users/user.js:168 -> controllers/usersController.js:176-199 (xxe).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: idorUpdateProfile() takes `req.query.id` directly from the request and calls usersController.updateUserById(req.body, req.query.id) with no check that the id belongs to the authenticated req.user. Any logged-in user can modify any other user's profile (fullname/username/email/phone) by supplying an arbitrary `id` query parameter. The companion idorViewProfile() (line 204-215) has the same missing-ownership-check pattern for reading arbitrary profiles, as does updateProfile()/errorBasedSqli() at lines 27-47.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: registerUser() stores user.password directly into the `password` column with no hashing, and authenticateUser() (line 13-22) compares it to the submitted password in plaintext via the raw SQL string. utils/sha512.js defines a generateHash() helper that is imported in utils/passportLocalStrategy.js but never invoked anywhere in the codebase, confirming passwords are never hashed before storage or comparison.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message:
searchUserBlackList() only checks the username against isFromBlackListOfSqli() (a SQLi keyword blacklist), not against any XSS filter. When the searched user is not found, the raw, unfiltered `username` is concatenated into the HTML response ('

User ' + username + ' not present'). This is rendered without escaping via views/reflected-xss.ejs:65 (`<%- htmlResponse %>`), reached from req.body.username in routes/users/user.js:107 (POST /reflected-xss). A payload like `` contains no SQLi keywords and is reflected verbatim, executing in the victim's browser.

searchByName() (called from xss-exercise, routes/users/user.js:196) applies only custom_sanitizer_regex() to the 'not present' message, which uses a single non-global regex replace `<(\w+)\W+[\w]` that only strips the first match. utils/utility.js:7 documents a working bypass (`<<img|hscript>alert(1)</script>`). The result is rendered unescaped via views/xss-exercise.ejs:67 (`<%- htmlResponse %>`), yielding reflected XSS from req.body.username.

`fullName` (sourced from req.user.fullname, which is stored verbatim from the registration form in models/usersModel.js registerUser() with no sanitization) is rendered unescaped with `<%- fullName %>` on every authenticated page (also views/navigation.ejs:17). A user who registers with an XSS payload in the fullname field (e.g. `<script>...</script>`) will have it execute in the browser of anyone who views a page rendering the header/navigation while impersonating or alongside that account, i.e. persistent/stored XSS.
`fullName` is rendered unescaped via `<%- fullName %>`, mirroring views/body-header.ejs:34/42 — same stored-XSS sink for the unsanitized registration `fullname` field.

searchLogs() builds a RegExp directly from unsanitized user input: `new RegExp('(public\\[\\d+\\] +.*' + search + '.*)')`, then runs it against every line of a log file. Reached via req.body.search in routes/users/user.js:156 -> controllers/usersController.js:159-174 (regExInjection). An attacker can inject regex metacharacters to build a catastrophically backtracking pattern (e.g. nested quantifiers), causing the event loop to block indefinitely — a denial of service.

The express-session middleware is configured with a hardcoded, weak secret ('secrettobechanged') and `cookie: { httpOnly: false, secure: false }`. `httpOnly: false` makes the session cookie readable via `document.cookie`, so any of the confirmed XSS vulnerabilities in this app (see stored/reflected XSS findings) can be used to steal the session cookie directly; `secure: false` allows the cookie to be sent over plaintext HTTP.

Database connection settings fall back to hardcoded default credentials ('127.0.0.1'/'database'/'user'/'pass') whenever the corresponding environment variables are not set, i.e. this app can silently run against a database using a hardcoded default password.

`new Buffer(userCookie)` uses the deprecated, unsafe Buffer constructor. Also relevant: utils/utility.js:139 `new Buffer(data, 'base64')` in getDeserializeData, feeding the node-serialize RCE sink above.
